what: Behind the cell, a Stripe-style mesh gradient flows slowly like paint — a plane twice the cell height is finely divided at .06 across and .16 down cells/px, and each vertex is pushed up by 3D simplex noise (frequency 3·4, speed 10·flow 3) to make waves (strength amp, default 320px), and three accent colors are layered over a deep accent background at noise thresholds .1 → .70·.77·.84 raised to the 4th power. When pinned it fades in from transparent in .8s power2.out, and it pauses off screen (200px margin). The cell shape (triangle·circle) is cut by the user with clip-path

options.amp: Wave strength pushing the panel (px), default 320 — over Brand: top triangle 450 · circle 400 · bottom triangle 500
options.seed: Noise seed — so the same layout looks different across several copies, default 5 (Brand 5·17·31)
options.speed: Overall speed (per ms), default 5e-6 (Brand original 8e-6 · lower 4e-6)
options.vspeed: Speed at which waves change, default 10 (brand 14·8)
options.vflow: Speed at which waves flow sideways, default 3 (reference site 4.5·2.5)
options.delay: Delay before turning on (sec), default 0 — Brand starts 1s after the loader clears
options.--fx-mesh-1 ~ 4: Three base and overlay colors (via style or css). By default they are --kf-accent turned darker, lighter and toward orange, plus --kf-accent-soft. When the skin changes, send fx:recolor to the element so they are re-read

note: The original uses MiniGl (a gradient port) — our WebGL code was newly written with the same plane, noise and layer values. The simplex noise is a public implementation (MIT)

from.where: index.html large shapes on the right of the hero (top triangle · circle · bottom triangle — amp 450·400·500, seed 5·17·31, speed 5e-6·8e-6·4e-6, vspeed 10·14·8, vflow 3·4.5·2.5, switched on 1s after the loader clears with .8s power2.out)
